source_text: EccLestA enim [et quidem] per universum orbem usque ad fines terre [dis|seminata, et ab Apostolis, et discipulis eorum accepit eam fidem, que est in unum Deum, Patrem omnipotentem, qui fecit colum et terram, δὲ mare, et omnia quo $n eis sunt: et in unum Christum Jesum filium Dei, incarnatum pro nostra salute: et in Spiritum Sanctum, qui per Prophetas predicavit de ex dispositiones Dei, et adventum, et eam, qus est ex Virgine generationem, et passionem, et resurrectionem a mortuis, et in carne in ccelos ascensionem dilecti Jesu Christi Domini nostri, et de colis in gloria Patris adventum ejus, ad recapitulanda universa, et resuscitandam omnem earnem humani generis, ut Christo Jesu Domino nostro, et Deo, et Salvatori et Regi, secundum placitum Patris invisibilis omne genu curvet colestium, et terrestrium, et. infernorum, et omnis lingua confiteatur ei, et judicium justum in omnibus faciat: spiritalia quidem nequitia», et angelos transgressos, atque apostatas factos, et impios, et injustos, et iniquos, et blasphemos homines in sternum ignem mittat: justis autem et quis, et prsecepta ejus servantibus, et in dilectione ejus perseverantibus, quibusdam quidem ab initio, quibusdam autem ex poenitentia, vitam donans incorruptelam loco muneris conferat, et claritatem seternam circumdet. . Hance preedicationem cum acceperit, et hanc fidem, quemadmodum przediximus, Ecclesia, et quidem in universum mundum disseminata, diligenter custodit, quasi unam domum inhabitans: et similiter credit iis, videlicet. quasi unam animam habens et unum cor, et consonanter hsc prsdieat, et docet, et tradit, quasi unum possidens os. Nam etsi in mundo loquele dissimiles sunt, sed tamen virtus traditionis una et eadem est. Et neque he que in Germania sunt fundats ecclesise, aliter credunt, aut ahter tradunt: neque hz que in Hiberis sunt, neque he que in Celtis, neque hx quse in Oriente, neque hx que in neque he que in Libya, neque he qus in medio mundi sunt constituts: sed sicut sol creatura Dei in universo mundo unus et idem est; sic et 5(lumen,) preedicatio veritatis, ubique lucet, et illuminat omnes homines, qui volunt ad cognitionem veritatis venire. Et neque is qui valde prevalet in sermone, ex iis qui preesunt ecclesiis, alia quam hsec sunt dicet: nemo enim super magistrum est: neque infirmus in dicendo deminorabit traditionem, Cum enim una et eadem fides sit, neque is qui multum de ea potest dicere ampliat, neque is qui minus deminorat. Pius autem aut minus secundum prudentiam nosse quosnon in eo quod argumentum immutetur, efficitur, et alius Deus excogitetur preter fabricatorem, et factorem, et nutritorem hujus universitatis, quasi non ipse sufficiat nobis, aut alius Christus, aut alius Monogenes: sed in eo, quod omnia quz in parabolis dicta sunt exquirere, et adjungere veritatis argumento, et in eo, ut instrumentum et dispositionem Dei in genere humano factam enarrat: et quoniam magnanimus extitit Deus, et in transgressorum angelorum apostasia, et in inobedientia hominum, edisserere; et quare alia quidem temporalia, alia vero sterna, et quedam coelestia, qusedam terrena unus et idem [Deus] fecit, annunciare: et quare cum invisibilis sit, apparuit Prophetis Dei [Deus] non in una forma, sed aliis aliter, adesse: et quare testamenta multa tradita humano generi, annunciare, et quis sit uniuscujusque testamentorum character, docere: et quare conclusi omnia in incredulitatem Deus, ut universis misereatur, exquirere: et quare Verbum Dei caro factum est, et passus est, gratias agere: et quare in novissimis temporibus adventus Fili Dei, hoc est in fine apparuerit. et non in initio, annunciare : et de fine et de futuris, qu&ecunque posita sunt in Scripturis, revolvere: et quare desperatas Gentes cohzredes et concorporatas et participes Sanctorum fecit; Deus, non tacere: et quemadmodum mortalis cc caro eis ravra et corruptibile incorruptelam. annunciare et quemadmodum factus [/. fatus] est Qui non erat populus, populus : et dilecta, dilecta; et quemadmodum Plures filii ejus deserta est, magis quam ejus que habet virum, preconare. talibus enim et in similibus eis exclamavit, Apostolus: O a/titudo dieitiarum et sapientie οἱ agnitionis Dei! quam inscrutabilia Judicia ejus, et investigabiles eia gus. Sed non in eo, ut supra Creatorem et Fabricatorem, matrem ejus et illorum, Enthyerrantis adinvenires, et ad tantam pervenires blasphemiam: neque in eo quod est super hanc rursus Pleroma, aliquando quidem xxx. aliquando vero innumerabiles dines ZEonum mentiri: quemadmodum dicunt hi. qui vere sunt deserti a divina sententia magistri; cum ea, qus est Ecclesia universa, unam et eandem fidem habeat in universo mundo, quemadmodum prediximus’.
pass_a_gloss: For the Church has indeed throughout the whole world and to the ends of the earth received from the Apostles and their disciples this faith, which is in one God, the Father, Almighty, who made heaven and earth, and the sea, and all that are in them; and in one Christ Jesus, the Son of God, incarnate for our salvation; and in the Holy Spirit, who through the Prophets preached the dispositions of God, and the advent, and the generation from the Virgin, and the passion, and the resurrection from the dead, and the ascension in the flesh to the heavens of the beloved Jesus Christ our Lord, and the coming from the heavens in glory of the Father, to recapitulate all things, and to resuscitate every flesh of the human race, so that every knee of heavenly and earthly and infernal things may bow to Christ Jesus our Lord and God and Savior and King, according to the pleasure of the invisible Father, and every tongue may confess to Him, and He may make a just judgment in all things; indeed, He will send spiritual wickedness, and angels who have transgressed and become apostates, and the impious, and the unjust, and the iniquitous, and blasphemous men into eternal fire; but to the just and those who keep His precepts and persevere in His love, to some indeed from the beginning, to others however from repentance, He will give incorruptible life as a reward, and will surround them with eternal glory. When the Church has received and has this faith, as we have said before, and is indeed dispersed throughout the whole world, it carefully keeps it, as if inhabiting one house; and similarly it believes in these things, as if having one soul and one heart, and it preaches and teaches and hands down these things in harmony, as if having one mouth. For although the languages in the world are different, yet the power of tradition is one and the same. And neither do those who are in Germany, nor those who are in Spain, nor those who are in the Celts, nor those who are in the East, nor those who are in Libya, nor those who are in the middle of the world, believe or hand down otherwise; but just as the sun, the creature of God, is one and the same in the whole world, so also the light of the truth of the preaching shines everywhere and illuminates all men who wish to come to the knowledge of the truth. And neither will he who is very powerful in speech, among those who preside over the churches, say anything other than these things; for no one is above the Master; nor will the weak in speaking diminish the tradition, for when the faith is one and the same, neither does he who can say much about it increase it, nor does he who can say less diminish it. But it is pious to know and to speak about these things, not so that the argument may be changed, and another God may be invented besides the Creator and Maker and Nourisher of this universe, as if He were not sufficient for us, or another Christ, or another Only-begotten; but so that all the things that have been said in parables may be sought out and added to the argument of truth, and so that the instrument and disposition of God, which has been made in the human race, may be narrated; and because God is magnanimous, to declare why the angels transgressed and became apostates, and why men were disobedient; and why some things are indeed temporal, others however eternal, and some heavenly, others earthly, one and the same God has made; and why, although He is invisible, He appeared to the Prophets of God, not in one form, but in different forms to different ones; and why many testaments have been given to the human race, to announce and to teach what is the character of each of the testaments; and why God has concluded all things in unbelief, so that He may have mercy on all; to seek out why the Word of God was made flesh and suffered; and why in the last times the advent of the Son of God, that is, at the end, has appeared, and not at the beginning; and to discuss the end and the future things, whatever has been put in the Scriptures; and why God has made the desperate nations co-heirs and co-corporal and participants of the Saints; and not to be silent about how mortal and corruptible flesh has been made incorruptible; and how He who was not a people has been made a people, and the beloved, beloved; and how the many sons of God have been deserted, more than she who has a husband, to preach. For in such things and similar things, the Apostle has exclaimed: O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are His judgments, and His ways past finding out. But not in the sense that one may go beyond the Creator and Maker, and invent a mother of Him and of these, and arrive at such blasphemy; nor in the sense that one may lie about the Pleroma, sometimes thirty, sometimes indeed innumerable divine Aeons, as those say who are truly deserted by the divine sentence of the Master; since the whole Church has one and the same faith throughout the whole world, as we have said before.

pass_b_english: The Church, spread throughout the whole world to the ends of the earth, has received this faith from the Apostles and their disciples. It is the faith in one God, the Father Almighty, who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them; and in one Christ Jesus, the Son of God, incarnate for our salvation; and in the Holy Spirit, who through the Prophets proclaimed the dispositions of God, the Advent, the Virgin birth, the Passion, the Resurrection from the dead, and the bodily Ascension into heaven of the beloved Jesus Christ our Lord. The Spirit also proclaimed His coming from heaven in the glory of the Father to recapitulate all things and to raise every flesh of the human race, so that every knee in heaven, on earth, and under the earth may bow to Christ Jesus our Lord, God, Savior, and King, according to the will of the invisible Father, and every tongue may confess to Him, and He may execute just judgment over all (Philippians 2:10-11). He will send spiritual wickedness, the angels who transgressed and became apostates, and the impious, unjust, iniquitous, and blasphemous men into eternal fire; but to the just and those who keep His precepts and persevere in His love—whether from the beginning or through repentance—He will give incorruptible life as a reward and surround them with eternal glory.

Having received this preaching and faith, as we said before, the Church dispersed throughout the whole world guards it carefully, as if inhabiting one house. She believes these things as if having one soul and one heart, and she preaches, teaches, and hands them down in perfect harmony, as if possessing one mouth. Although the languages of the world differ, the power of the tradition is one and the same. The churches in Germany do not believe or hand down otherwise, nor those in Spain, nor those among the Celts, nor those in the East, nor those in Libya, nor those in the center of the world. Just as the sun, God's creature, is one and the same over the whole world, so the light of the true preaching shines everywhere and illumines all who desire to come to the knowledge of the truth.

No leader powerful in speech will say anything other than these things, for no one is above the Master; nor will one weak in speech diminish the tradition. Since the faith is one and the same, he who can say much about it does not increase it, and he who can say little does not diminish it. Rather, it is pious to know and speak of these things—not to alter the argument and invent another God besides the Creator, Maker, and Nourisher of this universe, as if He were not sufficient for us, or another Christ, or another Only-begotten—but to seek out all things spoken in parables and join them to the argument of truth; to narrate the instrument and disposition of God wrought in the human race; and because God is magnanimous, to declare why the angels transgressed and became apostates, and why men were disobedient; and why the one and same God made some things temporal, others eternal, some heavenly, others earthly; and why, though invisible, He appeared to the Prophets not in one form but differently to different ones; and why many testaments were given to the human race, to announce and teach the character of each; and why God has consigned all to unbelief, that He may have mercy on all; to seek out why the Word of God became flesh and suffered; and why the Advent of the Son of God appeared in the last times, that is, at the end, and not at the beginning; and to unfold the end and the future things set in the Scriptures; and why God made the desperate nations co-heirs, co-corporal, and partakers with the Saints, and not to be silent about how mortal and corruptible flesh has been made incorruptible; and how He who was not a people was made a people, and the unloved, beloved; and how the children of the desolate woman are more numerous than those of her who has a husband, to proclaim. For in these and like matters the Apostle cried out: "O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments, and His ways past finding out!" (Romans 11:33). But not so that one may go beyond the Creator and Maker and invent a mother for Him and for these things, arriving at such blasphemy; nor so that one may lie about the Pleroma—sometimes thirty, sometimes innumerable divine Aeons—as those say who are truly deserted by the divine sentence of the Master; since the whole Church throughout the world holds one and the same faith, as we said before.

review.notes: Pass B fails to accurately translate the Latin text regarding the comparison of the desolate woman and the husband. The Latin reads 'et quemadmodum Plures filii ejus deserta est, magis quam ejus que habet virum, preconare' (and how more of his sons are desolate than she who has a husband, to proclaim/preach). Pass B translates this as 'and how the children of the desolate woman are more numerous than those of her who has a husband', which changes the subject and the meaning of the comparison. Additionally, Pass B translates 'et dilecta, dilecta' (and beloved, beloved) as 'and the unloved, beloved', which is a contradiction/error not supported by the Latin text.
reasons: Pass B translates 'et dilecta, dilecta' as 'and the unloved, beloved', which contradicts the source 'et dilecta, dilecta'.
